publish.title: The two-minute rule: clear tiny tasks fast
publish.description: A simple rule from Getting Things Done, with examples and its limits.

scenes.headline: Do it in two minutes
scenes.narration: Your to-do list is full of tiny tasks that do not belong on a list.

scenes.headline: The two-minute rule
scenes.narration: David Allen suggested a simple rule in his book Getting Things Done. If a task takes less than two minutes, do it right away.

definition.meaning: If a task takes less than two minutes, do it right away instead of adding it to a list.

scenes.headline: Good candidates
scenes.narration: Reply to a quick message, put a dish in the dishwasher, file a receipt, or book that appointment.
items: Put a dish in the dishwasher

scenes.headline: Why it works
scenes.narration: Tracking a tiny task takes about as long as doing it. Finishing it also clears your head.

scenes.headline: Watch the limits
scenes.narration: Do not let tiny tasks eat your whole day. Batch them, and protect time for work that matters.

scenes.headline: Do one now
scenes.narration: Think of one two-minute task and do it before this video ends.
